tutorial.title: DELETE Requests
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to use a DELETE request to send data to a server

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent: We use the DELETE method to remove a resource from the server, like deleting a file or record.

lessons.title: DELETE
lessons.interactiveContent:
DELETE is a request method that we use to delete existing data from the server, like a course Mimo wants to remove.

Make sure to pick DELETE.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Remove the existing course 10 from the server.

Make sure to pick DELETE.

lessons.title: DELETE URL
lessons.interactiveContent:
DELETE relies on a URL containing the server address, along with the type of resource that should be deleted.

Make sure to pick mimo.org.
lessons.hardModeContent:
DELETE relies on a URL containing the server address, along with the type of resource that should be deleted.

Target course 10 in the courses resource on mimo.org.

Make sure to pick mimo.org, followed by courses.

lessons.title: DELETE URL 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
This DELETE request's URL tells us that this existing piece of data should be deleted from courses.

Make sure to pick / followed by courses and then /, 10.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Target ID 10 in the courses resource for deletion.

Make sure to pick /, followed by courses, /, and finally 10.

lessons.title: DELETE URL Query Parameters
lessons.interactiveContent:
Like GET, DELETE requests usually do not have a request body, as the resource is identified by the URL.

Make sure to pick /, followed by 10.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Like GET, DELETE requests usually do not have a request body, as the resource is identified by the URL.

Identify course 10 with its ID as the last path segment.

Make sure to pick /, followed by 10.

lessons.title: Question: DELETE
lessons.interactiveContent:
What do we use DELETE requests for?

For deleting existing data from the serverFor retrieving data from the server

For deleting existing data from the server.
lessons.hardModeContent:
DELETE requests remove existing data from a server.

A user clicks Remove next to an existing article. Which request method should the browser send?

DELETEGETPOST

Make sure to pick DELETE.

lessons.title: Question: DELETE URL
lessons.interactiveContent:
How does the browser know where to send the data in the DELETE request?

Through the server address in the request's URLBy reading the data that the request is sending

Through the server address in the request's URL.
lessons.hardModeContent:
For DELETE https://api.example.com/articles/12, what tells the browser which server and resource should receive the request?

The URL https://api.example.com/articles/12The word DELETE aloneA request body that identifies article 12

The URL https://api.example.com/articles/12.

lessons.title: Question: DELETE URL 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Looking at this URL, what might the data we're sending be related to?

Deleting the article with the id 485A new user that signed up

Deleting the article with the id 485.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A request is DELETE https://fakenews.com/article/485. Which resource is targeted?

The existing article whose id is 485Every article on fakenews.comA new article with id 485

The existing article whose id is 485.

lessons.title: Example: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code an HTTP request method that deletes data from a server.

Make sure to pick DELETE.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Remove article 112 from the server at fakenews.com.

Make sure to pick DELETE, followed by fakenews.com.

lessons.title: Example: DELETE URL
lessons.interactiveContent:
Send a DELETE request to a server at fakenews.com.

Make sure to type DELETE.

lessons.title: Example: DELETE URL 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Through the DELETE request's URL, let the server know that the data you specify should be deleted.

Make sure to pick / followed by article and then /, 485.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Delete ID 485 from the article resource on fakenews.com.

Make sure to pick /, followed by article, /, and finally 485.

lessons.title: PUT Body
lessons.interactiveContent:
DELETE requests look very similar to GET requests in Express.

Make sure to pick delete.
lessons.hardModeContent:
DELETE requests look very similar to GET requests in Express.

Make sure to pick delete.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Typically, when using DELETE, we include an identifier in the URL as a route parameter.

Create an endpoint to delete a specific user from the database.

Make sure to pick / followed by users and then /, :id.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Typically, when using DELETE, we include an identifier in the URL as a route parameter.

Create an endpoint to delete a specific user from the database.

Make sure to pick /, followed by users, /, and finally :id.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
DELETE requests often rely on route parameters to identify the specific resource that should be deleted.

We use req.params.id to unpack a route parameter with the name id.

Make sure to pick req followed by . and then params, ., id.
lessons.hardModeContent:
DELETE requests often rely on route parameters to identify the specific resource that should be deleted.

Use req.params with the parameter name shown in the route.

Make sure to pick req, followed by ., params, ., and finally id.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
DELETE requests typically don't contain data in their request body, as the resource to be deleted is usually identified by the URL.

We can still access the body of the request object; however, most likely, it will be undefined.

Make sure to pick req, followed by .body.
lessons.hardModeContent:
DELETE requests typically don't contain data in their request body, as the resource to be deleted is usually identified by the URL.

You can still read the request body. In this example, no body was sent, so its value is undefined.

Make sure to pick req, followed by .body.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Similar to other methods, we can and should send back a response.

Make sure to pick res, followed by ., and finally send.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Send back plain text confirming which user ID was deleted.

Make sure to pick res, followed by ., and finally send.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy - Copy -
lessons.interactiveContent:
The default status if everything goes according to plan and the requested element is deleted is 204 No Content.

This indicates that the deletion was successful, and there is no content to return.

Make sure to pick ., followed by status(204).
lessons.hardModeContent:
The default status if everything goes according to plan and the requested element is deleted is 204 No Content.

This indicates that the deletion was successful, and there is no content to return.

Make sure to pick ., followed by status(204).

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy - Copy -  - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can also return 200 OK along with a response.

Make sure to pick . followed by status(200) and then ., send, `User with id ${userId} deleted`.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can return 200 OK with a response. Send plain text that identifies the deleted user by userId.

Make sure to pick ., followed by status(200), ., send, and finally `User with id ${userId} deleted`.

lessons.title: Question: PUT Body
lessons.interactiveContent:
Where do DELETE requests usually store the data they send to the server?

In the request bodyIn the URL

In the URL.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which request makes it clear that the server should remove the user with id 7?

DELETE /users/7DELETE /users with { id: 7 } in the bodyGET /users/7

Make sure to pick DELETE /users/7.

lessons.title: Example: PUT Body JSON
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a DELETE endpoint to delete a specific user.

Make sure to pick app followed by . and then delete, "/users/:id".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Register an endpoint to remove a user, using a route parameter named id under /users.

Make sure to pick app, followed by ., delete, and finally "/users/:id".

lessons.title: Question: POST Body 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
What might this DELETE request want from the server?

To delete a comment on an articleTo update a comment on an article

To delete a comment on an article.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A request is DELETE https://fakenews.com/article/112/comment/49. After it succeeds, what should no longer exist?

Comment 49 on article 112Article 112 and all of its commentsA new comment on article 49

Make sure to pick Comment 49 on article 112.

lessons.title: Example: POST Body 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Set the correct status code.

Make sure to pick 204.
lessons.hardModeContent:
204 No Content confirms success without a response body.

Finish the deletion with that status and no body.

Make sure to pick res, followed by 204.

lessons.title: Example: POST Headers
lessons.interactiveContent:
Send back a response along with the correct status code.

Make sure to pick res followed by . and then status, (, 204, ), ., send.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use the no-content success status after deletion and finish the response without a body.

Make sure to pick res, followed by ., status, (, 204, ), ., and finally send.
